sources.content:
## Overview

Persisted Work Context lets permitted participants inspect a Software Factory work order and its supporting evidence without relying on a live agent connection. It provides a shared reference for discussion and later review while preserving the source record's identity and access boundaries.

This is the standalone foundation for the first collaboration slice. It does not require a spatial interface or a selected orchestration vendor. This draft follows the [@project direction](https://factory.8090.ai/project/e6c7fbf5-1f8a-4427-a320-c9eaad5ff200/knowledge-base/e826fcd7-5b7f-402b-8fb8-8bcbef02b83a) and [@foundation research](https://factory.8090.ai/project/e6c7fbf5-1f8a-4427-a320-c9eaad5ff200/knowledge-base/9333ac71-1805-4b7a-92d4-406f6988be0a).

## Terminology

* **Participant:** an authenticated human or identified agent acting within granted project permissions.
* **Software Factory:** the existing project service that owns the source work records and their access rules.
* **Work Order:** a Software Factory record identifying a unit of tracked work, its description and current status.
* **Supporting Record:** a requirement, blueprint, knowledge resource or persisted conversation explicitly linked to a Work Order and available through supported interfaces.
* **Work Context:** the inspectable representation of a Work Order and its accessible Supporting Records.
* **Context Revision:** an identifiable saved state of the evidence presented in a Work Context, used to distinguish what a participant actually inspected from later changes.
* **Draft Contribution:** a participant's unsent text associated with one Work Context, distinct from a saved source record or submitted review.

## Requirements

### Work Context

### REQ-PWC-001: Open a permitted Work Order

**User Story:** As a Participant, I want to open a Work Order's context, so that I can understand the work before contributing.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

* **AC-PWC-001.1:** When a Participant opens a permitted Work Order, the Work Context shall identify its source project, Work Order identifier, title, description, current retrieved status, accessible Supporting Record references and last successful retrieval time.
* **AC-PWC-001.2:** While initial retrieval is incomplete, the Work Context shall indicate that it is loading.
* **AC-PWC-001.3:** If the Work Order has no Supporting Records, then the Work Context shall indicate that none are linked.
* **AC-PWC-001.4:** If the Work Order does not exist, then the Work Context shall indicate that it is unavailable.
* **AC-PWC-001.5:** If retrieval fails, then the Work Context shall offer a retry without representing the attempt as successful.
* **AC-PWC-001.6:** When the Work Context opens, the Work Context shall default to persisted evidence rather than imply live execution visibility.

### REQ-PWC-002: Inspect supporting evidence

**User Story:** As a Participant, I want to inspect linked Supporting Records, so that I can distinguish evidence from assumptions about the work.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

* **AC-PWC-002.1:** When a Participant selects an accessible Supporting Record, the Work Context shall expose its title, source reference, available saved content and retrieval freshness.
* **AC-PWC-002.2:** If a Supporting Record cannot be retrieved, then the Work Context shall mark that evidence as unavailable without hiding other retrieved evidence.
* **AC-PWC-002.3:** If retrieved content is incomplete, then the Work Context shall identify the omission rather than present the partial content as complete.
* **AC-PWC-002.4:** When further portions of accessible content are requested, the Work Context shall preserve the Work Order association while exposing those portions.
* **AC-PWC-002.5:** The Work Context shall distinguish source-record statements from Participant contributions.

### REQ-PWC-003: Recognize changed context

**User Story:** As a Participant, I want to recognize changes to the context I inspected, so that I do not make decisions against silently replaced evidence.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

* **AC-PWC-003.1:** When a Work Context is successfully retrieved, the Work Context shall identify the Context Revision presented to the Participant.
* **AC-PWC-003.2:** When a Participant requests refreshed evidence, the Work Context shall identify any detected change from the previously displayed Context Revision.
* **AC-PWC-003.3:** If a refresh fails while earlier evidence remains available, then the Work Context shall identify the retained evidence as not refreshed.
* **AC-PWC-003.4:** When refreshed evidence replaces earlier evidence, the Work Context shall preserve the association of earlier contributions with their original Context Revision.
* **AC-PWC-003.5:** If current source freshness cannot be verified, then the Work Context shall disclose that limitation.

### REQ-PWC-004: Protect context access

**User Story:** As a Participant, I want my access boundaries respected, so that collaboration does not expose records I am not permitted to inspect.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

* **AC-PWC-004.1:** If a Participant lacks access to a Work Order, then the Work Context shall withhold its protected content.
* **AC-PWC-004.2:** If a Participant lacks access to a Supporting Record, then the Work Context shall withhold that record's protected content.
* **AC-PWC-004.3:** When access revocation is detected, the Work Context shall stop exposing the affected protected content in subsequent interactions.
* **AC-PWC-004.4:** If a Participant follows a shared Work Context reference, then the Work Context shall apply that Participant's permissions rather than the sender's permissions.
* **AC-PWC-004.5:** The Work Context shall not grant source-record write access merely because a Participant can view the context.

### Draft Contribution

### REQ-PWC-005: Preserve an unsent contribution

**User Story:** As a human Participant, I want to leave and return to my unsent contribution, so that an interruption does not discard my work.

**Acceptance Criteria:**

* **AC-PWC-005.1:** When a Participant begins a Draft Contribution, the Work Context shall associate it with that Participant, Work Order and Context Revision.
* **AC-PWC-005.2:** When a Draft Contribution is saved, the Work Context shall indicate its saved state.
* **AC-PWC-005.3:** If saving fails, then the Work Context shall indicate that the latest text is not confirmed saved.
* **AC-PWC-005.4:** When the same Participant returns after navigation or refresh, the Work Context shall restore the last confirmed saved Draft Contribution subject to current permissions.
* **AC-PWC-005.5:** If the underlying Context Revision has changed, then the Work Context shall mark the restored Draft Contribution as based on earlier context.
* **AC-PWC-005.6:** When a Participant chooses to discard a Draft Contribution, the Work Context shall require confirmation before removing its saved text.
* **AC-PWC-005.7:** If another session changes the same saved Draft Contribution, then the Work Context shall expose the conflict without silently discarding either saved text.
* **AC-PWC-005.8:** The Work Context shall default to keeping Draft Contributions private to their author until explicitly submitted.
* **AC-PWC-005.9:** When a Participant explicitly requests saving a Draft Contribution, the Work Context shall persist that text subject to current permissions.
* **AC-PWC-005.10:** If a Draft Contribution exceeds 10,000 characters, then the Work Context shall reject saving with the size limit identified.
* **AC-PWC-005.11:** If a save fails, then the Work Context shall retain the attempted text in the current session for recovery.
* **AC-PWC-005.12:** The Work Context shall default to explicit draft saving rather than imply that unsaved text is durable.

## Scope Boundaries

Included: inspectable persisted context, evidence provenance and freshness, permission boundaries, and preservation of unsent human contributions. Draft preservation is not a promise of in-flight agent checkpointing.

Excluded: creating or rewriting source Work Orders; automated source-status transitions; spatial presence; live agent events; hosted-agent invocation; hidden reasoning access; in-flight steering; external messaging/calling; model/skill evaluation experiments. Those capabilities require separate requirements and verified interfaces.

## MVP Defaults

Source refresh is manual. Draft saving is explicit, with a 10,000-character limit; recovery guarantees apply to confirmed saved text. Source content is disclosed as partial when incomplete and may be fetched in additional portions without changing the reviewed evidence silently. The first slice does not promise live events, automatic refresh, or cross-device draft synchronization. No automatic deletion of saved drafts or review evidence is included in this slice; a retention and deletion policy is required before production deployment.

The implementation uses supported source access only. A fixture-backed demonstration must be labeled as demonstration data and must not claim verified live access. Dependency choices and implementation contracts belong in the paired blueprint.

sources.content:
# Persisted Work Context

## Feature Summary

This targets [@Persisted Work Context requirements](https://factory.8090.ai/project/e6c7fbf5-1f8a-4427-a320-c9eaad5ff200/requirements/ca86c93a-63ed-4996-888e-c46147f3a186): open permitted work, inspect evidence, identify changed context and preserve private saved drafts. The connected repository implements a persisted fixture foundation and, as of 2026-11-14, a bounded server-side Factory API evidence adapter with a verified real source-change stale-review rejection in [PR #6](https://github.com/dryprogrammer/sf-evolve-2026/pull/6). The contracts below remain the full target architecture: current selectable demo personas and API-key-creator scope do not satisfy production authentication or per-participant source authorization; no live hosted-agent or Factory-to-app MCP round-trip is delivered.

## Architecture Diagram

```mermaid
flowchart LR
  U[Participant] -->|open, refresh, save| P[Work Context Presenter]
  P -->|context reads| C[Context Service]
  P -->|draft commands| D[Draft Service]
  C -->|supported reads| S[Source Adapter]
  S -->|per-principal access| SF[Software Factory API]
  C -->|immutable snapshots| DB[(Collaboration Store)]
  D -->|versioned writes| G[Command Repository]
  G --> DB
  C --> A[Access Policy]
  D --> A
```

## Component Blueprint Composition

[@Collaboration Access and Persistence](https://factory.8090.ai/project/e6c7fbf5-1f8a-4427-a320-c9eaad5ff200/blueprints/e94f7650-5260-426c-a9d3-1b3685f21fee) owns #AccessPolicy, #CommandRepository and #CollaborationStore. #ContextService uses authorization and immutable persistence; #DraftService uses author-scoped command receipts and optimistic concurrency. The shared components are configured for this work/evidence scope, not redefined here.

## Feature-Specific Components

```component
name: SourceAdapter
container: Factory App
responsibilities:
	- Implement `SourceReader` through supported APIs with server-side per-principal credential mapping.
	- Preserve pagination, source identities, versions and individual linked-record access outcomes.
	- Normalize missing, denied, partial, failed and unverified results without filling gaps silently.
	- Supply a separate fixture implementation for tests and labeled offline demonstration.
```

#ContextService calls #SourceAdapter for a permission-filtered evidence manifest. Denied content and credentials never enter client projections; source text remains untrusted data.

```component
name: ContextService
container: Factory App
responsibilities:
	- Create immutable `ContextSnapshot` records from work identity and evidence actually exposed.
	- Compute canonical evidence digests excluding retrieval times and pagination cursors.
	- Preserve prior contribution associations when refresh or additional portions create a new revision.
	- Produce server-side `EvidenceVerification` for approval against the round's exact evidence manifest.
```

#ContextService stores snapshots in #CollaborationStore and returns `ContextView` to #WorkContextPresenter. #DraftService associates saved text with that snapshot so refresh cannot silently rebase contributions.

```component
name: DraftService
container: Factory App
responsibilities:
	- Save, restore and discard `DraftContribution` for its verified author only.
	- Use #CommandRepository for expected-version writes, retry reconciliation and conflict reporting.
	- Enforce contribution limits and distinguish confirmed saved state from attempted text.
```

```component
name: WorkContextPresenter
container: Factory App browser client
responsibilities:
	- Present source work identity, description, status, evidence references, revision and retrieval time.
	- Distinguish loading, empty, partial, denied, failed and retained-not-refreshed states with manual retry.
	- Keep attempted text in session on save failure, restore confirmed drafts and confirm discard.
	- Separate source evidence from contributions and display fixture provenance.
```

```model
name: ContextSnapshot
store: Postgres
description: Immutable record of evidence presented for one source work item.
fields:
	- id: UUID (primary key)
	- projectId: string (required)
	- workOrderId: string (source identifier)
	- evidenceDigest: string (canonical evidence digest)
	- manifest: JSON (source identities, versions, fetched content boundaries, access and completeness)
	- retrievedAt: timestamp (display only, excluded from digest)
	- sourceMode: enum (live, fixture)
constraints:
	- Immutable after creation; never contains credentials.
	- Historical evidence reads recheck permissions on every supporting record.
```

```model
name: DraftContribution
store: Postgres
description: Private saved text associated with the context inspected by its author.
fields:
	- id: UUID (primary key)
	- projectId: string (required)
	- workOrderId: string (required)
	- authorId: string (trusted principal)
	- contextSnapshotId: UUID (required reference)
	- text: string (maximum 10,000 characters)
	- version: integer (optimistic concurrency)
	- updatedAt: timestamp (required)
constraints:
	- Author-only read/write subject to source permission.
	- Conflicts leave confirmed text unchanged and return attempted text to its author.
	- Discard does not alter source work or review history.
```

## System Contracts

### Key Contracts

* REQ-PWC-001/002 map to #SourceAdapter, #ContextService and #WorkContextPresenter. REQ-PWC-003 maps to snapshots/change reporting; REQ-PWC-004 to #AccessPolicy; REQ-PWC-005 to #DraftService and #CommandRepository.
* `SourceReader` operations are readWork, listLinkedEvidence, readEvidencePortion and verifyManifest. Upstream routes/fields come from current official documentation, not guesses. Adapter failures remain explicit.
* Loading additional evidence creates a new snapshot instead of altering an existing snapshot. Denied or incomplete evidence is visible as such, never represented as fully reviewed.
* Approval verification checks every item in the published manifest using supported version IDs or complete canonical content comparison. Newly linked evidence, changed versions, missing portions, denial or unverifiable results prevent an unchanged verification result.
* Participants may have different source visibility. Historic projections recheck permissions; stored content from a privileged user's snapshot is not permission for others. Publication requires a manifest accessible to the assigned humans.
* Explicit saves use expectedVersion and idempotencyKey. Failures preserve confirmed persisted state and in-session attempted text. Never-saved text has no browser-crash durability guarantee.
* Refresh is manual. Retained old evidence is marked with its last successful retrieval time. Detected permission revocation clears affected protected content from subsequent projections.

### Integration Contracts

* `ContextView`: project/work identity, title, description, sourceStatus, snapshotId, evidenceDigest, retrievedAt, supportingReferences, completeness, freshness and sourceMode.
* `EvidenceVerification`: snapshotId, verifiedAt, result (`unchanged`, `changed`, `unverifiable`), changedReferences and incomplete/denied references; produced server-side, never accepted as client proof.
* Draft commands carry work/snapshot IDs, text, expectedVersion and idempotencyKey. Author identity comes from #AccessPolicy. Conflicts return only the caller's confirmed draft/version.
* UI regression tests use the persisted fixture backend; adapter/store contract tests use explicitly labeled fake source readers. A separate live proof retrieves actual Factory records and changes only a labeled supplemental demo document. `FACTORY_SOURCE=api` is opt-in server-side evidence access under `FACTORY_MODE=fixture`, with separate storage/scope; the API key remains in secure environment settings. Production identity and per-user access validation remain gates, not achieved requirements. No key enters browser projections, logs or committed environment files.

## Architecture Decision Records

### ADR-001: Keep source work authoritative in Software Factory

**Context:** Mirroring all work into another orchestration ledger adds reconciliation and separate compute budgets.

**Decision:** Read source work through #SourceAdapter; store only snapshots, private drafts and local review state. Never change source status implicitly.

**Consequences:** Asynchronous inspection/review does not require external agent inference. Gas City remains a future adapter candidate, not a required runtime.

### ADR-002: Compare evidence, not refresh timestamps

**Context:** Refresh times must not invalidate unchanged review while actual content must not change beneath contributions.

**Decision:** Hash canonical identities, content, source versions and completeness; exclude retrieval metadata and preserve immutable snapshots.

**Consequences:** Unchanged evidence can be reverified in the same round; actual changes or additional content create a new revision. No atomic consistency across external source records is claimed.

### ADR-003: Limit the first executable source adapter to fixtures

**Context:** A repository is now connected, but supported per-user Software Factory authentication has not been verified. A source connection for indexing is not permission to impersonate each application user.

**Decision:** The first implementation uses immutable fixture source evidence, canonical key-sorted digests stable through PostgreSQL JSONB serialization, archived snapshots, explicit private draft saves and simulated change/outage/revocation controls. There is no external source API request or live source credential in this pilot. Confirmed drafts are author-scoped and versions remain monotonic after discard. Expected fixture persona is checked before mutation, and detected source-permission loss clears protected browser state.

**Consequences:** The pilot validates context/draft interaction and transactional recovery without claiming real access enforcement. Live source authentication, arbitrary project/work selection, supporting-record pagination and production authorization remain gaps before the feature satisfies its full requirements. See the repository README for implemented-versus-deferred scope.

### ADR-004: Add bounded authoritative evidence without upgrading demo identity

**Context:** The owner authorized the API/MCP follow-on and selected native UI on the existing private PR #6 branch. External API health, selected work-order reads, directly linked requirements/blueprint reads and exposed revision metadata were verified. Factory-to-app MCP registration/reachability was not established.

**Decision:** The bounded #SourceAdapter implementation uses supported `GET /work_orders/{uuid}`, `GET /requirements/{uuid}`, `GET /blueprints/{uuid}` and `GET /artifacts/{uuid}` with a server-side project API key. Evidence covers full selected-work Markdown, all directly linked requirements/blueprints/document-backed Knowledge Base resources, plus explicitly configured supplemental demo documents. Two matching complete reads form a bounded stable cut; canonical content digests supplement available revision IDs. Missing, denied, unsupported, incomplete or unstable evidence fails closed. #ContextService persists source observations separately from immutable saved/round snapshots and reverifies before local mutations; old approval/sign-off bases remain stale after refresh. API and fixture storage scopes are separate, and API-backed work rejects fixture simulation commands. The application exposes no source-write API; the explicitly opted-in localhost proof runner edits only its exact labeled non-sensitive probe.

**Consequences:** Actual Factory probe revision A → B changed the local saved basis from `501d786b52c258a758ed25eba53b026255371fa67f362ee853f708691e1e8322` to `fc269dc15123d444e82639299311bf53c236bb4c3c422328fa656a1b0320c83f`; approval of the old signed round returned HTTP 409 `changed_evidence` before and after refresh, and a fresh demo review required fresh sign-off. [PR #6](https://github.com/dryprogrammer/sf-evolve-2026/pull/6) retains sanitized proof and independent mock/fixture tests. This proves Project Driver local enforcement, not native Factory approval, production human authentication or independent multi-person review. The API key acts as its creator; per-participant source grants, arbitrary work selection, partial pagination, transitive records/comments/code and atomic cross-record consistency remain outside this slice. A Factory agent → app MCP → attributed actual human answer → retrieved/used agent output remains deferred pending supported custom registration and authenticated private ingress; no human answer or protocol completion is fabricated. ADR-003 records the earlier fixture-only checkpoint rather than the current source adapter.

sources.excerpt: /** Server-only, project-key-scoped read adapter. No write API or caller-selected URL. */

reviews.name: Intent reviewer
reviews.summary: The blueprint broadly serves the requirement's goal of inspecting persisted work context and preserving private drafts. It also adds approval and sign-off verification, which the requirement never defines.

findings.title: Blueprint adds approval/sign-off scope beyond the requirement's goal
findings.claim: In this snapshot, the requirement's goal is persisted context inspection and private drafts, with source-status automation excluded. The blueprint also builds approval verification and sign-off enforcement, and the requirement has no acceptance criteria for either.

citations.quote: It provides a shared reference for discussion and later review
Excluded: creating or rewriting source Work Orders; automated source-status transitions;
Produce server-side `EvidenceVerification` for approval against the round's exact evidence manifest.
a fresh demo review required fresh sign-off

findings.uncertainty: The requirement mentions "later review" and a "submitted review", so approval may be an intended follow-on. It lists neither approval nor sign-off as included or excluded. Other requirements outside this snapshot may cover them.
findings.correction: Either add approval and sign-off requirements, or mark the approval verification and sign-off parts of the blueprint as out of scope for this feature.

reviews.name: Delivery reviewer
reviews.summary: The PR #6 adapter delivers a bounded, read-only, server-side Factory evidence read, but it handles an unretrievable linked record by rejecting the whole read. That differs from the original scope, which asks for per-record unavailable states that keep the other evidence visible.

findings.title: Adapter fails the whole read instead of marking one record unavailable
findings.claim: In this snapshot, the requirement and blueprint call for per-record outcomes, with an unretrievable Supporting Record marked unavailable while other evidence stays visible. The collected adapter code calls invalid() for any unsupported or failed linked record, which aborts the whole read. It also hardcodes every returned evidence item as complete and permitted. So it delivers all-or-nothing verified evidence, not partial or denied states per record.

citations.quote: If a Supporting Record cannot be retrieved, then the Work Context shall mark that evidence as unavailable without hiding other retrieved evidence.
Preserve pagination, source identities, versions and individual linked-record access outcomes.

findings.uncertainty: Only the adapter file is in the snapshot. A presenter or service layer that is not collected here might still show per-record states. The fail-closed behavior may also be an intentional choice for review-mutation safety, since the adapter's own error text says cached evidence cannot authorize a review mutation. The snapshot does not include tests or the callers of this adapter.
findings.correction: Have the adapter return a per-record outcome (available, unavailable, denied or partial) for each linked record instead of calling invalid() for the whole read. Keep the fail-closed rule only where a review mutation needs fully verified evidence. If the all-or-nothing behavior is intended for this slice, record it explicitly as a deviation from the original requirement.

reviews.name: Skeptic
reviews.summary: The PR #6 adapter plausibly delivers a bounded, read-only evidence foundation. The collected requirement, blueprint and code do not show that it satisfies per-participant permission semantics for Persisted Work Context.
reviews.dissent: I do not dispute that the adapter is a reasonable, fail-closed, read-only slice. I dispute only treating it as evidence of the original requirement's access behavior. The requirement asks for per-Participant permissions, and the code reads with one project-key scope.

findings.title: Project-key adapter is not per-participant access enforcement
findings.claim: REQ-PWC-004 requires shared references to use the viewing Participant's permissions. The blueprint expects per-principal credential mapping. The PR #6 adapter is described as project-key-scoped, so the collected code does not show the original access requirement is met. An alternative reading is that the adapter is an intentionally narrower pilot and the stronger behavior is deferred.

citations.quote: If a Participant follows a shared Work Context reference, then the Work Context shall apply that Participant's permissions rather than the sender's permissions.
Implement `SourceReader` through supported APIs with server-side per-principal credential mapping.
Server-only, project-key-scoped read adapter. No write API or caller-selected URL.

findings.uncertainty: The snapshot has only the adapter file, not the rest of the application, tests or access-policy layers. Per-participant checks could exist elsewhere. The blueprint also says the current scope does not satisfy production authorization, so this may be a known deferral rather than an undisclosed defect.
findings.correction: Describe the adapter as bounded project-key evidence retrieval. Do not claim REQ-PWC-004 or per-participant authorization is satisfied until the principal-to-credential mapping and per-record access outcomes are implemented and tested.
